teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Gather students on a nature walk around the schoolyard. Discuss the importance of numbers in counting items found outdoors.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Encourage students to observe their surroundings and think about what they might be able to count.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Provide students with small bags and ask them to collect different natural items (e.g., stones, leaves, flowers).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: After collecting items, students will work in pairs to count their objects and write down how many of each they found on a worksheet.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guide students to create a class chart on a whiteboard to display the number of each item collected by all students.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Each pair will present their findings, sharing how many of each object they counted, reinforcing counting and number recognition.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.learning_activities: Present prepared model, attempt quizzes and participate in interview
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explain what a number line is and its use in organizing numbers in order. Show a simple number line on the board.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Discuss why number lines are useful and where they might see them in real life, such as on a ruler or a clock.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Provide various everyday items (buttons, straws, or blocks) for students to use and demonstrate how they can make their own number lines on the floor or on large paper.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will arrange their objects in order according to a number line they create, being sure to label it from 0 up to 10 or 20.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Once completed, each group will have a turn to present their number line to the class.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Encourage students to share how they arranged their objects and any challenges they faced. They can discuss how they can extend their number line with more objects for larger numbers.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explain the scavenger hunt concept and how numbers appear in many places, such as on houses, signs, and license plates.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Have students brainstorm where they might find numbers in school or at home.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Create a list of numbers for students to find around the school (e.g., the number of classrooms, windows, stairs).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will be divided into small groups and given 30 minutes to go around the school to locate and record the different numbers they find.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Once the scavenger hunt is complete, gather students to discuss and share their findings.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Each group will present one interesting number they found, explaining where they found it and what it signifies (e.g., "Room 5 indicates the fifth classroom").
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Display several types of objects collected from the environment (e.g., leaves, stones, or paperclips). Ask students how they think we could group these items.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Allow students to suggest various methods for sorting the objects (by color, size, or type) and discuss why sorting is useful.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guide students in sorting the objects into groups, teaching them how to count the quantity in each group.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will take turns creating their grouped categories and calculating the total in each category, such as We have 7 green leaves and 3 brown leaves.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Together, create a visual display of the sorted items on a chart paper that includes pictures or drawings and numbers representing the counts.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will write a reflection about what they learned from the sorting activity and how counting helped them organize items efficiently.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Discuss various habitats (grocery store, park, home) and the significance of numbers within them. Ask what kinds of observations they might make related to numbers.

teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Create a worksheet with spaces for various categories, like Number of trees in the park or Items in a grocery cart.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will go to different stations around the school to observe and fill out their worksheets with numbers related to their observations.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Upon returning to the classroom, facilitate a discussion where students can share their observations and the numbers they found during the activity.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Each student will create a small presentation to illustrate one observation they made, including an explanation of why that number was significant.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Concept of numbers are mastered

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Introduce numbers 1 to 20 using a number chart displayed in the classroom. Sing a counting song that includes these numbers.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will follow along, counting together aloud. Encourage them to point at the numbers on the chart as they sing.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Distribute worksheets with a list of numbers in numeral form (1 to 20) and leave a space for students to write the word form beside each numeral.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will fill in the spaces with the corresponding word forms (e.g., 1 - one, 2 - two), using the number chart as a reference.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Organize a small group discussion where students can share their favorite numbers from 1 to 20 and why they like those.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will present their completed worksheets, and the teacher will provide feedback and reinforce correct numeral-word associations.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Review numbers 1 to 20 briefly. Introduce numbers 21 to 50 and explain the pattern in how these numbers are formed with "twenty-one," "twenty-two," etc.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will listen and repeat after the teacher as numbers are read aloud, practicing pronunciation of the new numbers.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Create a matching game where numeral cards (21-50) are paired with corresponding word cards.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: In pairs, students will match the numeral cards to the correct word cards, taking turns reading both the numeral and the word.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Conduct a class review to discuss the pairs they created and resolve any discrepancies.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Each student will choose three pairs to report back to the class to reinforce learning. They can create a mini-poster displaying the chosen numbers in both forms.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.learning_activities: Ask students to identify any patterns they notice in the way the numbers are formed.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Provide students with a handout that lists numerals and corresponding spaces to fill in the word forms. Begin with 51 through 60.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will work independently to fill in the missing words and then check with a partner for accuracy.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Organize a classroom number line activity where students will stand in order based on the numbers they have completed in word form.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will write a reflective paragraph on what they noticed about the patterns from 1 to 100, incorporating specific examples from their fill-in activities.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explain the rules of Bingo and how the game will help them practice their numbers from 1 to 100.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Show an example Bingo card and explain how to fill in the squares with both numerals and words.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Provide each student with Bingo cards with a mixture of numerals and words from 1 to 100.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Call out numbers in word form and have students cover the corresponding numeral on their cards or vice versa. Continue until someone shouts "Bingo!"
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: After the game, discuss the winning numbers to reinforce the numeral and word connections among peers.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Students will write down five numbers they got during Bingo and practice writing both the numeral and word for homework.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Numbers in numerals and words are identified (1-100)

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Compile all the pages into a class number book and organize a book launch in which students can share their pages with classmates and even younger students.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Hand out worksheets that have the numbers 1 to 5 in a dotted format, allowing students to trace over the numbers.
